title: SLO synthesis, golden signal signatures and pager-governor for noise-resilient alerting
creator: Aisha Moreno
description: Goal: Reduce noisy/false positive pages by building a lightweight SLO synthesis layer that derives 'golden signal' signatures from trace/metric/log fusion and drives a pager-governor that applies context-aware suppression and graded escalations.
background: We continue to see elevated page noise on tail-latency regressions originating from transient upstream flaps and cold-cache bursts. Existing burn-rate alerts fire broadly and trigger immediate paging for P1 SLOs. Postmortems show ~35% of those pages were actionable within 15 minutes; the rest were transient and caused unnecessary oncall disruption. This ticket scopes the engineering work to create a synthesis service that enriches alerts with trace signatures, recent change-context (deployments/capacity), and anomaly score to make paging decisions more noise-resilient.
acceptance_criteria: Synthesis service produces a 'golden_signature' hash for each SLO breach event within 150ms of alert ingestion
Pager-governor enforces suppressions for events with high transient score and applies graded escalation windows (silent->ops-chat->page) configurable per-SLO
Integrations: tracing hooks publish span attributes used for signature; metrics pipeline tags SLO windows; logs pipeline extracts recent deploy IDs and error-rates
End-to-end tests validating: a simulated cold-cache spike is suppressed (no page), a sustained latency spike triggers page after configured window
Dashboard: New SLO alerting view showing suppressed vs paged events, signature histogram and suppression rationales
Docs: Runbook and config reference added to Confluence + changelog entry for oncall team
work_notes: 2026-03-10 - Kickoff: scoped minimal viable synthesis prototype. Decided to use a Bloom-filter-like stable hashing for golden_signature to tolerate noise in span ordering.

2026-03-11 - Design review with Observability PMs: agreed synthesis inputs = (service, endpoint, 95th latency bucket, recent deploy id, top-3 exception types, trace-sampled-span-signature). PM requested ability to opt-out per-customer for Private deployments.

2026-03-12 - Prototype implementation: added trace hook to runtime sidecar that emits compact span fingerprint (sha1 of normalized span op + top attr keys). Instrumented pipeline to join fingerprints with metric SLO events in our ingest kafka topic.

2026-03-13 - Bench results: signature gen adds 18ms p95 to ingest path when run inline; moved to async enrich worker to meet 150ms end-to-end requirement. Still validating memory overhead for high-cardinality services.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): tracing hook + async signature generator, alert enrichment service, pager-governor with simple suppression policy (transient-score threshold)
Phase 2: incorporate anomaly-detector ML model for transient scoring, expose per-customer policies, add UI controls in Console for suppression tuning
Phase 3: A/B rollout and telemetry-driven policy tuning (evaluate reduction in pager rate and missed-actions)
open_questions: What privacy constraints for Private deployments? PM requested signatures be reversible for debugging; security prefers one-way stable hash. Need legal input.
Should suppression be time-boxed only, or include traffic-aware throttles (e.g., suppress if system-wide noise spike detected)?
Anomaly model placement: run in-stream (low-latency) vs batch scoring (higher fidelity). Tradeoffs: latency vs accuracy.
risks: Incorrect suppression tuning may increase time-to-detect real outages (false negatives)
High-cardinality services could blow up signature index size; need TTL and sampling heuristics
Added complexity in paging flow might confuse oncall; require clear UI and runbook updates
progress_updates: 2026-03-11 - Tracing hook spec landed in design doc. @emma reviewed and asked for clearer privacy controls for Private mode.
2026-03-12 - Prototype PR opened: observability/service-enricher#1287 (WIP). CI failing on memory test for signature cache size.
2026-03-13 - Moved signature generation to background worker to reduce ingest tail latency; integration tests passing locally.
review_feedback: PM (Jonas): prefer conservative default suppression settings; expose a 'fast-page' override for SLOs tied to customer-facing payments flows.
Design (Emma): dashboard mockups look good; add a 'why suppressed' inline tooltip that surfaces recent deploy and top-span examples.
SRE (Hannah): require a kill-switch feature that disables suppression globally for 30 minutes after major incidents.
next_steps: Stabilize prototype memory footprint and add TTL eviction for signature cache
Add Confluence draft of runbook for oncall and suppression tuning guidelines
Schedule A/B test for two customer cohorts in Stage environment
